data.completion_memo: Made `fallback_tool_id` platform-independent. It now takes the final path component by splitting on both `/` and `\` (`workflow_path.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next()`) and derives the stem from that component, so `D:\wf\Krea-2_Turbo_T2I_Upscale_API.json`, `/home/me/wf/Krea-2_Turbo_T2I_Upscale_API.json` and a bare `Krea-2_Turbo_T2I_Upscale_API.json` all yield `krea-2-turbo-t2i-upscale-api` on every OS. The test now asserts all three forms plus the existing no-name and 64-char bound cases. Verified: `cargo test --lib fallback_ids_are_identifier_safe_and_bounded` passes on Linux, `cargo check --all-targets` reports no warnings, and the full desktop `cargo test --lib` suite is now 629 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (the previously failing platform test is green).

lines: `fallback_tool_id` in desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/service/comfyui.rs derived the id with `Path::new(workflow_path).file_stem()`. That only treats `\` as a separator on Windows, so a Windows workflow path read on Linux produced `d-wf-krea-...` instead of `krea-...`; the unit test `fallback_ids_are_identifier_safe_and_bounded` therefore always failed on non-Windows.

Fix: split the path on both `/` and `\` on every platform (`rsplit(['/', '\\'])`) and derive the stem from the final component, so a path frozen on any platform yields the same id. Extend the test with a POSIX path and a bare file name that must both match the Windows case, and keep the no-name and 64-char bound cases.

data.title: Make the ComfyUI fallback tool id derive the same id from any platform's path
